parts.text: State the magnitude and unit of absolute zero on the thermodynamic temperature scale.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why temperature measured using a laboratory liquid-in-glass thermometer does **not** give a measurement of thermodynamic temperature.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain how Fig. 2.2 shows that platinum is a suitable metal for use in a resistance thermometer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest a reason why a platinum resistance thermometer is **not** suitable for measuring a rapidly changing temperature.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest a type of thermometer that is suitable for measuring a rapidly changing temperature.

parts.text:
A negative temperature coefficient thermistor may be used as a type of resistance thermometer.

State **one** way in which the variation with temperature of the resistance of a thermistor differs from that of a platinum wire.
